title: Canary rollout retrospective and change-window checklist
content:
Attendees: Mariana (RE), Ethan (SRE), Priya (serving-runtime), Jonah (observability), Samira (release ops)
Meeting date: 2026-03-10 14:00 PT / 2026-03-10 21:00 UTC
Purpose: quick retro after last week's canary rollout (v2026.03.04) + consolidated change-window checklist for next scheduled rollout. Focused on minimizing blast radius for model-serving changes and tightening the rollback playbook.

High-level summary:
- Canary rollout completed to 5% traffic over 60m, then 25% over next 40m, then ramp to 100% after automated checks passed.
- Observed small but measurable uptick in 95th percentile token latency on one dedicated pool (gpux-13) during the 25% stage (+24% vs baseline). No customer-facing errors.
- Two errors surfaced: transient KV cache miss contributing to a retry loop (INF-3456) and a stale feature-flag in the autoscaler path causing slower scale-ups (INF-3472). Both reverted within the canary window and did not reach 100% rollout.
- Lessons: need earlier kernel-level telemetry surfaced in the canary dashboard and a documented quick-toggle for autoscaler feature-flag.

Timeline (short):
- 09:50 PT: Pre-roll checklist validated (see checklist below).
- 10:00 PT: 5% traffic -> automated perf suite (smoke + small prompt set).
- 10:50 PT: 25% traffic -> anomaly detected in gpux-13 95p latency. Alerts triggered (alert ids: latency-95p-gpux-13, retry-loop-3m).
- 11:05 PT: Rollback of model variant on gpux-13 to previous kernel candidate.
- 11:12 PT: Autoscaler feature-flag toggled off for cluster autoscaler path; scale events normalized.
- 11:30 PT: Canary stabilized at 25% with mitigations; decision: continue ramp with extra monitoring.
- 12:15 PT: Full rollout scheduled but deferred to next change window pending root-cause analysis.

Root cause notes (working):
- KV cache miss pattern: correlated with garbage-collection spike on gpux-13 nodes (kernel v1.12.1). Likely regression in memory accounting for model kv-shard eviction. Ticket INF-3456 created with heap/GC traces and kernel binary.
- Autoscaler FF: stale rollout config allowed autoscaler to prefer capacity from a lower-priority pool; slowdown during scale-up. FF toggle existed but not surfaced in runbook. Ticket INF-3472 created to add explicit runbook step and make FF toggles visible in Console.

Impact matrix:
- Customer latency: no SLA breaches, but internal 95p latency goal (<= 180ms token gen) was exceeded on gpux-13 by ~24% for 18 minutes.
- Error budget: negligible burn.
- Operational load: SRE/RE teams spent ~40m handling mitigation.

Monitoring gaps identified:
1) Canary dashboard lacks kernel-level GC/eviction counters per node. (ACTION: Jonah to add GC metric panels; due 2026-03-17)
2) Autoscaler FF toggles not surfaced in rollout UI; runbooks don't call out FFs as checklist items. (ACTION: Priya + Samira to update runbook + UI change request; PR and runbook draft due 2026-03-19)
3) Alert threshold tuning: retry-loop alert fired at 3m of sustained retries — want a staged alert (1m warning, 3m critical). (ACTION: Ethan to update alert rules; due 2026-03-16)

Change-window checklist (canonical for next rollouts) — must be completed and ticked before stepping beyond 25%:
- Owners assigned and on-call pages verified (yes/no) -> MUST verify within 30m pre-roll.
- Smoke test suite: small prompts + long-context synthesis + embedding hash checks -> green.
- Canary dashboards: latency, p50/95/99, token throughput, retry loops, kernel GC, KV miss rate, mem/cpu by node.
- Feature-flag audit: list of FFs affecting autoscaler/eviction must be enumerated.
- Rollback artifacts: exact previous model binary tag, kernel candidate, and infra-args must be pre-registered in release bundle.
- Communication: Slack channel pinned, pager escalation plan confirmed, customer-notify template prepared if user-visible impact.
- Approval gate: RE lead + SRE on-call must approve move past 25%.
- Time-window confirmation: production change window (UTC): 14:00–18:00 UTC preferred for APAC overlap; alternative 02:00–06:00 UTC for low-traffic maintenance.

Quick rollback playbook (short form):
1) If retry loops or 95p latency > threshold for > 5m: hold ramp to next stage and notify RE + SRE.
2) If service-level errors (5xx) > 0.5% for > 3m: immediate blue/green rollback to previous model version and kernel.
3) If node-level GC/eviction spike correlates with a kernel candidate: revert kernel on affected pools and isolate nodes from canary.
4) Clear audit and post-rollback verification: run smoke suite, re-check dashboards for 20m.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Jonah: Add kernel GC + KV-eviction panels to canary dashboard; include node filtering by pool. Due 2026-03-17.
- Ethan: Implement staged retry-loop alert (warning 1m, critical 3m) and annotate alert runbook. Due 2026-03-16.
- Priya + Samira: Update release runbook to include FF audit step, add quick-toggles section, and add a one-click rollback checklist in Console. Draft PR: infra#487. Runbook update due 2026-03-19.
- Mariana: Triage INF-3456 with runtime traces and coordinate kernel rollback candidates. Due 2026-03-15.
- Jonah + Priya: Draft a short post-rollout communication for customers describing mitigation and that no user data was affected. Due 2026-03-18.

Follow-ups and next meeting:
- Short sync 2026-03-12 10:00 PT to confirm runbook edits and alert changes are merged.
- Full retrospective with additional engineering teams 2026-03-20 to do a deeper dive on memory/accounting changes impacting gpux pools.

Notes / informal scribbles:
- Consider adding a lightweight "canary smoke runner" that executes kernel-heavy synthetic prompts to exercise KV/eviction before traffic ramp. Prototype idea: small job that runs on candidate nodes for 10m at 5% CPU.
- We should keep a named list of tolerant vs sensitive models for canary routing; some models are highly latency-sensitive and should either be isolated or use a stricter gate.
- Question: should we split canary by pool type (gpux-old vs gpux-13) rather than uniform sampling? Pros: isolates hardware regressions. Cons: slower signal for global regressions.

References & links (quick):
- INF-3456 (kv cache misses + GC traces)
- INF-3472 (autoscaler FF repro + config)
- Canary dashboard (Console -> Deployments -> Canary 2026-03-04)
- Slack: #release-ops thread ABC123 (archived)
- Runbook stub: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RELEASE/pages/123456/Release+runbook+stub

Appendix: brief template for customer communication (copy/paste):
Subject: Brief update on last model rollout (March 4)
Body: We rolled a model update to production in a staged canary. During the canary we detected an internal performance regression on a subset of GPU hosts which we reverted within the canary window. There was no user-visible downtime or data exposure. We have implemented mitigations and are conducting a deeper review; we will share a follow-up with root-cause details and timeline for the stable rollout. If you want more details or run extra validation on your tenant, please reply and we'll prioritize.

-- End notes --
